title: Exception: Image upload failed due to loss of GPU access on iOS Devices on 3.27.1

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
In my production app, I have some asset images that fail to display once the issue is triggered, despite having already displayed properly:

```
Image(
    image: AssetImage('some/image/path.png'),
    width: size),
    height: size
)
```

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: I'm also getting this using native flutter Image.asset() on flutter 3.27.1, while it used to work with previous versions. I looked at the linked comment, but was unsure how to apply what it was saying to avoid doing this. comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Thanks for the detailed report and analysis of potential root-cause @reporter 

you're welcome!

> Since `extended_image` is third party package, does the same behavior exhibit using Image.network ? 

I don't see it with `Image.network` (though I haven't tested extensively) but I do see it with Flutter's `AssetImage`.
It also affects `vector_map_tiles` (reporter/flutter-vector-map-tiles#228)

> Also, does [this](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/159397#issuecomment-2512414995) comment help further in your case as why it could be occuring ?

The comment suggests that the application is trying to load or decode images while in the background, but that's not what's happening here.
In all cases, the application has already loaded the images but they appear to get unloaded (by the Flutter framework or the OS) when the application is put in the background. When the application is brought back to the foreground the error occurs.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: Hello all, I had this exact issue which I appear to have solved. The solution was actually rather simple, at the beginning of my build() function I initialized the image in an ImageProvider object, and then used this initialized variable in the returned widget. As someone who also has the goal of building a production level app, I sympathize with these types of little errors!

comments.author: participant28
comments.body:
Mine might be a special case but I resolved it so sharing.
I use a location plugin (flutter_background_geolocation) which opens the app in the background on iOS when it's tracking location and the app is then terminated. But then when the app is opened again, some of my images weren't showing and I got the error mentioned here.

My solution was to not show these images until the AppLifecycleState.resumed is seen (since when the app launches in the background the lifecycle state is AppLifecycleState.inactive and becomes AppLifecycleState.resumed when it's shown in the foreground by the user clicking on the app icon).

I've also been experiencing the same error with images that are already loaded into memory throwing exceptions when the app moves to the background. I can see the exception in the console before I even move the app back to the foreground.

I also ran git bisect, but I narrowed the problem down to commit 9a74329c15119078d38dec3e50a0e63e0364a49a, which seems to just bump the Impeller and Fuschia versions. Parent commit b883b2337d069de5f2e561bff59d084a9561e152 doesn't have this bug.

Rolling back to 3.24.5 fixes the issue in both my production app, so I'm moving forward with that version for now, but I just wanted to add my findings in case they could help solve the problem.

It's worth mentioning that I can't reproduce the bug in my production app in any stable release from 3.29.0 through 3.29.3, so I guess one of the attempted fixes at least partially solved my problem. Sounds like other people are still having the issue though.

To summarize my findings:

Last good commit before this bug: b883b2337d069de5f2e561bff59d084a9561e152
First bad commit exhibiting this bug: 9a74329c15119078d38dec3e50a0e63e0364a49a

Last good stable release before this bug: 3.24.5
First bad stable release exhibiting this bug: 3.27.0

comments.author: participant16
comments.body:
I'm not sure this is truly fixed

As I understand it, the current solution preserves only 64 images — the rest are discarded. While 64 might sound like a large number, it’s actually quite small in practice. In our app we have hundreds of images.

Consider a demanding use case like a social media app. Typically, there’s a user feed screen displaying many images. Based on this sample:(https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/161142#issuecomment-2724037180), it’s clear that images are being unloaded when the app is backgrounded and then resumed.

In such scenarios, the client shouldn’t have to refetch all images from the server every time the app is backgrounded — which can happen frequently, even every few seconds. With the current behavior, many images would appear unloaded, and the user has no option but to quit and relaunch the app to recover. Moreover, the unloading seems to happen arbitrarily — a friend reported seeing missing images even in the navigation bar, not just in the user feed.

comments.body:
But if I'm right, the issue isn't just about a better fixed number. No matter what limit is chosen, the problem will still occur:
1. For some apps like social media or chat apps, users load hundreds of images in a short session while using app.
2. They background the app and switch between others frequently.
3. On resume, main() isn’t called (only didChangeAppLifecycleState with resumed is triggered) so previously loaded images aren’t reloaded, resulting in empty placeholders. 
EDIT: Naturally, we can't re-fetch all images from the server every time the app resumes, nor can we can persist them in local cache.

comments.body:
**SAMPLE APP:**

Although I’m unable to implement this myself, here are clear instructions for setting up a simple sample project - something that should be quick to complete:
1. Start with a slightly more complex sample app that includes:
    - A navigation bar with asset-based images (not icons).
    - Two distinct screens, each accessible via the navigation bar.
2. On each screen, include a ListView that loads a large number of remote images using lazy loading or infinite scrolling. You can use the following API to fetch placeholder images: https://picsum.photos/

**Test Flow:**
1. Alternate between the two screens repeatedly to trigger image loading and navigation stack behavior. Load hundreds of images - a simple scrolling with a 3x3 grid, would load > 100 images in a few seconds.
2. Send the app to the background, then resume it:
    - Immediately.
    - After a delay of ~20 seconds.
This will better simulate a real-world usage scenario and help surface the issue under realistic conditions.

Thanks for the initial report and all the discussion on this issue. We've revisited the original reproduction code provided, and it appears that with current versions of Flutter, this specific issue is no longer reproducible as initially described in [code](
https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/161142#issue-2769500744).

To ensure our issue tracker remains focused on current, actionable bugs with clear reproduction steps, we will be closing and locking this particular issue.

**If you are still experiencing a similar problem related to image uploads and GPU access on iOS with a recent and stable version of Flutter, please file a new issue.**

When filing a new issue, please ensure you provide:
 
* A minimal, complete, and verifiable reproduction (MCVE) using the latest stable version of Flutter. This is crucial for us to investigate effectively.
* Any relevant error logs or console output

Providing a fresh, reproducible example allows us to address the problem in its current state without confusion from outdated information.

Thank you for your understanding and contributions to Flutter!
